dataset.description:
Recent years have brought exponential progress in the field of computational protein design, opening new
opportunities for optimizing proteins for multiple functions. One such path is designing proteins with high
binding affinity for specific targets. This is a promising path to develop therapeutic options to treat a broad
range of diseases, including viral infections and cancer. This progress is more notable on miniprotein (MP)
design: proteins with up to 100 residues that tend to have mostly helical folds. More recently, nanobody (NB)
design has undergone significant developments, with several packages showing higher success rates. However,
for some types of proteins, the existing tools have limited success in designing and selecting the most
promising candidates. Within this list, we can find monobodies (MOB). These proteins are small antibody-like
proteins derived from the Human Fibronectin type III, that have been increasingly leveraged in research for
oncological and virological applications.
With this HPC project, we aim to design, using AI/ML/DL and physical methods, protein binders with multiple
types of folds against a broad range of therapeutic targets (viral and oncological).
For the MP and NB design, well-established pipelines will be used to design protein binders for relevant viral
and oncological therapeutic targets. For the MOB design, we will adapt existing NB pipelines (given the
similarity of its structure to the MOB one) by fine-tuning their hyperparameters or adapting the pipelines to
generalize for MOB design. Multiple methods will be tested to generate tens of thousands of designs. The most
promising candidates will first be screened through yeast display to estimate the success rate of each approach
and select the candidates that bind to the target. These will be further characterized in in vitro and in vivo
assays, which in turn will inform us of the one method (or the multiple ones) that have higher success for the
different targets.
